commits.subject: 💚 Make the face and release tests pass on Windows

why: the face tests used the host's platform, and Ctrl-Z handling is off on Windows by design; the release test compared two scratch repos whose remote paths, with random suffixes, appear in the notes' links on Windows.

commits.subject: 📝 Correct the terminal section of the brand guide

why: BRAND.md described the code before the final review's fixes, and got a few details wrong.

commits.subject: 🐛 Treat every ssh "Permission denied (" as a credentials failure

why: an ssh server that offers only passwords failed the step instead of letting git ask for one.

commits.subject: 🐛 End a planning step warn when Jev left commits unsorted

why: a release whose every Jev batch failed still ended ✓, and the spec says exit 3 from next-version ends on "Nothing to release" too.

commits.subject: 🐛 Ask the terminal for its theme only from the foreground, and only once a face draws

why: `chamoji memory sync &` was stopped by SIGTTOU, and every face command paid up to 300 ms for a question most never needed.

commits.subject: 📝 Record the first real terminal check

why: the intro and the face were seen in one real terminal, and the plan should say plainly which terminals still need a look before the release.

commits.subject: 📝 Record the terminal face: brand, roadmap, readme and results

why: the face, the foil rule and the three environment variables need one place to be read from, and the byte-identity check against 0.11.0 is the evidence that stdout is untouched.

commits.subject: ✨ Add the animated welcome and regroup the help

why: a bare `chamoji` printed the whole reference to stderr and exited 2, which read as an error and gave no sense of what the tool is for. The new tagline is a draft and needs Alec's approval.

commits.subject: 🐛 Retry a quiet tag fetch, count a failed Jev and let Ctrl-C through

why: Under a face, a tag fetch that needed a password fell back to local tags without asking, a Jev that failed on its first request ended with a ✓, and Ctrl-C during the background query was swallowed.

commits.subject: ✨ Show faces in the commands that wait

why: memory sync, release, init and the rest went quiet while they waited on git, GitHub or Jev, so they looked stuck.

commits.subject: ✨ Add the face settings, gitStep and Jev's progress

why: The commands need to know when a face may animate, a way to run network git under a face without hiding a password prompt, and a count of Jev's batches to show.

commits.subject: 🐛 Leave ssh alone when GIT_SSH is set

why: GIT_SSH_COMMAND overrides GIT_SSH, so the quiet env would have replaced a user's own ssh program.

commits.subject: ✨ Report sync steps and keep network git quiet

why: The loading faces need to say which step a slow command is on, and a redrawing face must not overwrite a git password prompt.

commits.subject: 🐛 Keep partial text when the face first draws

why: Text written without a newline while a step waited was erased by the first frame when stdout and stderr share a terminal. The face now starts a new line first.

commits.subject: ✨ Add the face helper

why: Commands that wait need one place that draws the loading face on stderr and owns that line, so later wiring only has to wrap steps.

commits.subject: ✨ Add the wordmark frames and their generator

why: The terminal wordmark has to match what was approved, so a script renders the real Marow Block letters and the face as quadrant blocks, evens out the eyes by a pixel where quantising skews them, and only the generated strings are committed.

commits.subject: ✨ Add the one-line faces and the ASCII fallback

why: the spinner and ending lines need a fixed set of 7-column faces, and Windows consoles outside Windows Terminal cannot draw the Unicode set.

commits.subject: 🐛 Keep swallowing a late terminal reply

why: A background reply that arrived after 100 ms was echoed to the shell prompt, and a stray BEL ended the query before the real reply. The query now stays raw for a 200 ms grace window and only treats a BEL or ST after ESC]11; as the end.

commits.subject: ✨ Add the foil colour and theme detection

why: The terminal faces and the wordmark share one colour layer. It blends the seven foil stops, paints text through chalk at a set level, and finds out whether the terminal background is light or dark.

commits.subject: 🔧 Start the terminal face workstream

why: building it as a workstream gives the release one Highlights entry and keeps the dogfooding going.
